subject: Cross-provider quality triage and next benchmarks
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@polytech.ai>; Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Nov 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cross-provider quality triage and next benchmarks

Hi Sam — thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single plan going into the evaluation cycle.

Summary of where BluePeak landed on the call:
- Primary objective: validate model-quality parity vs your current provider for customer-facing summarization and KB retrieval workflows.
- Key concerns: hallucination on financial/legal entities, tail-case latency under 95th percentile SLAs, and reproducible regression checks for future rollouts.

Redwood differentiators (quick):
- Consistent inference performance across hosted + dedicated with automatic fallback to quantized variants for cost-sensitive runs.
- Prefix/KV caching that preserves conversational context without hurting tail-latency.
- Built-in eval hooks so you can compare outputs + token economics side-by-side.

Proposed test matrix (high level):
1) Quality sweep: run our curated prompts (attached: sample-eval-prompts.md) + your representative transcripts; record hallucination rates and factuality deltas.
2) Latency & cost parity: 1k synthetic user threads at your 95th percentile seq lengths vs your hyperscaler baseline (we'll run both hosted and a dedicated config).
3) Regression harness: seed a subset of prompts into our eval runner and snapshot outputs for automated regression checks.

What we need from you to start:
- A redacted sample of 100 transcripts (or synthetic equivalents) and the priority prompt subset (financial/legal focused is highest).
- Confirmation of whether the vendor eval team needs prompt IDs attached to outputs.
- Preferred window for the benchmarking sprint (we were thinking next week, Mon-Wed).

Attachments: [sample-eval-prompts.md (md)], will follow the detailed matrix (Ben will drop the spreadsheet).

If that looks right, I’ll have Ben put the matrix and pass/fail criteria into a shared sheet and we’ll lock a 30-min kickoff.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

--

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@polytech.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Nov 2028 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cross-provider quality triage and next benchmarks

Vanessa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifying points from our side before we hand over samples: 

1) Data handling & PII: our security team requires that any sample transcripts be redacted and that outputs do not get persisted in systems outside of a temporary eval bucket. We can share an S3 path with short TTL. Is that workable?

2) Prompt IDs: yes — the vendor eval team needs prompt IDs attached to outputs so we can map failures back to prompts in our scoring harness. Can your eval runner emit a CSV mapping?

3) Hallucination focus: we want to prioritize financial entity hallucination (company names, account numbers masked) and legal clause hallucination. If you can include a short variant set (3–5 paraphrases per prompt) that will help.

Available for a kickoff: Tues 11/7 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 11/8 14:00–15:00 PT.

Thanks — Sam
Sam Patel
Head of Vendor Evaluation, BluePeak Solutions
sam.patel@polytech.ai

Sam / team — I put a first-cut benchmark matrix into the shared sheet and mapped pass/fail criteria. Key pieces below; spreadsheet attached: cross-provider-sprint-matrix.xlsx

Quick definitions (so scoring lines up with your vendor team):
- Hallucination rate: percent of outputs with at least one unsupported factual assertion vs ground truth. Tolerance: <= 3% for Tier 1 prompts.
- Exact-match policy: for structured extraction only (numbers, account ids) we expect >= 98% token-level match after masking.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile token-gen latency < 350ms for our dedicated config at a steady state of 500 QPS.
- Cost delta: end-to-end token cost within 10% of your current hyperscaler baseline for equivalent config; we’ll show both raw token cost and normalized per-successful-response cost.

Proposed experiment schedule:
- Day 0: kickoff, exchange redacted samples and grant temp S3 access.
- Day 1–2: run quality sweep + paraphrase variants.
- Day 3: latency/cost parity run.
- Day 4: regression snapshot + output delivery.

Candidate kickoff slots (pick one):
- Tue 2028-11-07 10:00 PT
- Wed 2028-11-08 14:00 PT
- Thu 2028-11-09 09:30 PT

If you confirm a slot I’ll spin up the runs and share a dashboard with per-prompt deltas, hallucination highlights, and raw outputs (CSV exported with prompt_id column as requested).

Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

Thanks Ben / Vanessa — Wed 11/8 14:00 PT works for us (confirming the 11/8 slot). Couple of final items from our vendor team: 

- Please include a focused subset of 40 prompts that specifically stress financial entity hallucination and legal clause fabrication. We’ll add those to the sheet under the column "BluePeak-priority".
- We will provide a temporary S3 bucket (redacted transcripts + mapping file). Expect a separate email from eng-ops with the link and TTL.
- One ask on output format: include a small JSON line per output with fields {prompt_id, model_variant, output_text, hallucination_flags} — that will speed automated scoring on our side.

Looking forward to the kickoff. If you can send a calendar invite I’ll accept it and loop in our compliance reviewer for the first 10 minutes.

Sam
